title: Alphabet Stock, Amazon Stock, or Microsoft Stock: Which is the Best Beaten-Down AI Stock to Buy Now?
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions. Amazon's fair-value figure is garbled/missing in the captions; only the ~40% undervaluation is stated.
summary: Parkevtate Vosianc compares Alphabet, Amazon and Microsoft head-to-head after several consecutive days of selling, asking which is the best buying opportunity. He owns all three and wants to buy more of each. On earnings growth, analysts forecast Amazon at 23.6% per year, Microsoft 16.4% and Alphabet 13%, though he believes these estimates are understated because data-centre spending hits cash flow now while the earnings follow later. Free cash flow separates them sharply: Microsoft generated $60 billion over the trailing 12 months and is the only hyperscaler forecasting positive free cash flow in fiscal 2027, while Amazon is at negative $47 billion trailing 12 months with capital spending above $225 billion in 2026 and probably near $300 billion in 2027, and Alphabet is forecast negative in 2026 (-$10 billion) and 2027 (-$37 billion), turning only modestly positive in 2028. Forward price-to-earnings: Amazon 23, Microsoft 20, Alphabet 18. His discounted-cash-flow fair values are Alphabet $356 against a $273 price (about 30% undervalued), Microsoft $580 against $490 (about 18%), and Amazon roughly 40% undervalued. His verdict: Amazon is the best of the three and ranks among his top 10 stocks to buy, but all three are buying opportunities. Calls: GOOGL BUY at $273 (FV $356), AMZN BUY (~40% undervalued), MSFT BUY at $490 (FV $580); all reiterations.

calls.video_title: Alphabet Stock, Amazon Stock, or Microsoft Stock: Which is the Best Beaten-Down AI Stock to Buy Now?
calls.thesis: BUY reiterated (was BUY 7 Nov, FV $370 then — FV cut to $356). ~30% undervalued at forward P/E 18; EPS growth forecast 13%/yr, which he says is understated. FCF forecast negative 2026 (-$10B) and 2027 (-$37B) on aggressive AI data-centre spend, modestly positive 2028.
calls.base_case: Data-centre spend is a short-term burst; once Alphabet has enough capacity, spending drops and the cash-flow machine resumes.
calls.bull_case: EPS growth beats the 13% forecast as AI capex converts into income-statement earnings.
calls.bear_case: Heavy AI capex keeps free cash flow negative for two years and may require tens of billions in borrowing.
